name: Museum für Naturkunde
funding: In November 2018 the German government and the city of Berlin decided to expand and improve the building for more than €600 million.

name: Neue Nationalgalerie
funding: The German federal government and the federal states fund the Berlin State Museums, which include the Nationalgalerie.

name: Neuer Berliner Kunstverein (n.b.k.)
funding: The Berlin Senate Department for Culture and Social Cohesion and the Stiftung Deutsche Klassenlotterie Berlin fund it.

name: Oyoun
funding: The Supporting Act Foundation supports Oyoun with an Impact Grant in 2025 and 2026. A crowdfunding campaign pays legal and court costs.

name: SAVVY Contemporary: The Laboratory of Form-Ideas
funding: The Berlin Senate Department for Culture and Social Cohesion partly funds it. Public funding, private sponsorship, donations and contributions by SAVVY friends e.V. also finance it.

name: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin
funding: Federal government pays 71% of the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation's €275M operating budget, Berlin 14%, other Länder 7%. Sparkassen-Finanzgruppe is main sponsor, renewed in 2017.

name: Stiftung Stadtmuseum Berlin
funding: It is a public-law foundation created by state law in 1995.

name: daadgalerie
funding: The Federal Foreign Office and the State of Berlin fund the Berliner Künstlerprogramm, which shows work at the daadgalerie.

name: transmediale
funding: Annual festival (2026) funded since 2004 by the Kulturstiftung des Bundes. Berlin Senate, bpb, Medienboard and Creative Europe funding was listed for 2020 to 2021.

name: Kunstverein Bielefeld
funding: Nearly 1,000 members plus eleven corporate partners: Sparkasse Bielefeld, Hörmann, DMG MORI, Dr. Wolff, Gundlach, Bautra, Wannenmacher, Enderweit, jablgo, PGW Pecunia, Comspace.

name: Bonner Kunstverein
funding: Project funders: Kunststiftung NRW, NRW culture ministry, Kemmler Foundation, Art Explora.
